title: One-shot cancellation settles even when descendant discovery fails

categories.prompt: Start a one-shot shell command with a background child holding stdout open, then abort it. Descendant discovery is unavailable. Cancellation must terminate the owned command group and return a timeout result without executing the later shell command.

executableTestNames: stops the one-shot process tree when the tool call is aborted and process discovery fails
stops the one-shot process tree when the user stops it and process discovery fails
signals a shell before its children so it cannot go on to the next command

notes: The main macOS log shows an aborted-command timeout but does not log the underlying process lookup. Failed discovery is a deterministic reproduction of that failure mode. Real-shell regressions retain the original 8-second bound and clean up their own fixture processes even if an assertion fails.
